title: Add model family + version bucketing for Usage Insights reporting (aliases + deprecated models)
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
Usage Insights breakdowns currently key on a raw model identifier which is not stable across:
- aliases (e.g., marketing alias vs canonical catalog ID)
- model version naming changes
- deprecations / removed models

This causes duplicate rows in exports and makes week-over-week comparisons noisy.

Goal: introduce stable bucketing fields for reporting (model_family + model_version, plus canonical model ID) and ensure aggregation + query APIs can roll up consistently across aliases and deprecated models, while preserving the original model identifier for audit/debug.

Primary users: engineers + finops relying on route/model cost breakdown and CSV export; reconciliation must remain consistent vs billing totals.

References:
- Support: SUP-24844 (CSV export shows duplicate rows for model aliases)
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/in-console-usage-insights-prd.json
- ADR reference: confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-route-normalization-and-attribution.json (extend approach to model normalization semantics)
- Query service/API contract: confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/usage-insights-api-contract.json
acceptance_criteria:
1) Aggregated dataset(s) for Usage Insights include the following model dimensions:
   - model_canonical_id (stable internal ID, source-of-truth: model catalog)
   - model_display_name (human readable, may be alias)
   - model_family (stable family string used for reporting; ex: "llama-3.1", "qwen2.5", "mistral-small")
   - model_version (stable version identifier within family; allow "unknown" for historical gaps)
   - model_deprecation_status ("active" | "deprecated" | "removed")
   - model_alias_of (optional: canonical ID if event used an alias; empty if already canonical)

2) Aliases roll up into the same model_canonical_id bucket by default (no duplicate rows for the same canonical model in CSV exports when grouped by canonical).

3) Deprecated/removed models still appear in historical reporting with stable family/version fields populated (or explicitly "unknown") and are flagged as deprecated/removed.

4) Query API supports filtering and grouping by (model_canonical_id OR model_family/model_version) without breaking existing clients that filter by model string.

5) Backfill strategy documented for last N days (align with retention/backfill plan); correctness checks vs billing totals remain within tolerance.

6) Unit/integration tests cover:
   - alias -> canonical mapping
   - version parsing from catalog metadata
   - handling unknown models (events referencing old IDs)
   - deprecation status behavior

7) Data quality monitoring: emit metric for % of events with model_version == "unknown" and % of events with unmapped alias.
implementation_notes:
Proposed approach (agreed in #eng-platform thread 1737582207 follow-up):

A) Define a shared normalization function:
- Library: telemetry/model_identity (mirrors route normalization library approach)
- Input fields (from metering/telemetry events): model (raw), model_id (if present), deployment_mode, region
- Output: model_canonical_id, model_family, model_version, model_display_name, model_alias_of, model_deprecation_status

B) Source of truth:
- Pull canonical mappings from Redwood model catalog snapshot (daily) into warehouse table: dim_model_catalog_snapshot
- Include:
  - canonical_id
  - family
  - version
  - aliases[] (flattened into mapping table)
  - deprecation_status
  - effective_start / effective_end (optional; useful to freeze historical mapping)

C) Aggregation job updates (ENG-3812):
- Add new columns to route+model rollup dataset.
- Grouping default for insights UI should use model_canonical_id; retain model_display_name for presentation.

D) Query API updates (ENG-3814):
- Backwards compatibility: existing "model" filter continues to work by translating input into canonical_id where possible.
- New filters:
  - model_canonical_id
  - model_family
  - model_version
- Response includes both canonical and display fields.

E) Deprecated model behavior:
- If model is deprecated but still in catalog snapshot: keep mapping, set deprecation_status=deprecated.
- If model no longer exists in catalog snapshot (removed): set model_canonical_id to a deterministic hash bucket of raw model string, set family/version="unknown", deprecation_status="removed", and preserve raw_model for debug.

F) Known trade-offs:
- Canonicalizing at query-time vs aggregation-time: we will canonicalize at aggregation-time to prevent duplicate rows and keep query latency predictable.
- Mapping drift risk: freeze mapping by snapshot date per event_time partition (prefer snapshot as-of event day).

open_questions: Do we want UI grouping default to model_family (roll up across versions) or canonical model (family+version)? Current proposal: canonical by default, with an optional roll-up toggle in UI.
How should we display deprecated models in the console filter dropdowns (badge vs hidden unless explicitly searched)?
Should "removed" models be excluded from Top Cost Drivers cards by default to avoid confusing customers, or included with a warning tooltip?
definition_of_done: Merged schema + aggregation changes to include canonical model fields; query API updated with backward compatible filter semantics; backfill for last 14 days completed; reconciliation tests pass; dashboards show unmapped/unknown rates; SUP-24844 no longer reproducible on export.
